thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated inference p95 latency from az1b - spike in outbound queue length on a subset of ENIs, increased DNS timeouts and some 502s. Pager auto-triaged to infra.pager (severity: high).

sam (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing context. Which AZ exactly? any customer-facing symptoms reported yet?

incident-bot: Affected zone: az1b. Start: 2026-03-15T09:15:01Z. Alerts: ENI Rx queue depth > 75% on 12 hosts, resolver timeouts increased 5x, fronting NLB target failures observed. No SLO alerts yet but spikes in 95th latency.

olivia: Confirmed, I'm seeing elevated p95 for /v1/generate in metrics. Rolling 30s windows show spike ~09:12 -> 09:18. Traffic still flowing but tail latency up to 2.3s.

diego: Network infra note: just saw a partial egress queue pileup on the subnet that hosts unserenference-g5 pool. Could be ENI interruption or noisy neighbor. Pulling ENI stats.

sam (oncall): Diego, can you paste the `tc`/dmesg snippets? tagging @eng-sre-oncall for routing decisions.

diego: here's relevant output:

```
Mar 15 09:13:10 host-az1b-g5 kernel: net_rx: enp2s0f0: skb_trim: rx-queue-depth 512 -> 10240
Mar 15 09:13:11 host-az1b-g5 kernel: ENI RX drop: 34 drops/sec
Mar 15 09:14:05 host-az1b-g5 /usr/local/bin/eni-monitor: conntrack-saturation=warn
```

olivia: Also seeing resolver latencies from instances in az1b: `dig +time=2 +tries=1 api.internal.redwood: TTL 60, rtt 120ms` vs normal ~20ms. Could be control plane or AZ-level network jitter.

sam (oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) Mark affected hosts Out for NLB health to steer new inference requests away. 2) Increase cross-AZ fallback weight to eu-west2 for burst traffic. 3) Lower DNS TTL for api.internal to speed future failovers. 4) Coordinate customer comms. Start 1 and 2 now.

eng-sre-oncall: Agreed. I'm going to update NLB target group. Running: 

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-health-check --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --health-check-path /healthz --healthy-threshold-count 2 --unhealthy-threshold-count 1
for id in $(cat affected_instances.txt); do aws elbv2 deregister-target --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --target-id $id; done
```

sam (oncall): Doing DNS TTL now (reduce to 30s) and enabling route weight to eu-west2. Command to adjust fallback policy in control plane: `redwoodctl route set-fallback --region eu-west-2 --weight 0.25`

diego: Quick note — deregistering targets will cause some in-flight requests to be retried. prefer to drain gracefully: `deregister` then sleep 20s. set health-check to 3/1 for faster detection.

olivia: Started autoscaler pause on the g5 pool in az1b to avoid churn. `k scale deployment inference-g5 --replicas=0 --namespace=service` (we'll handle scale-up in other regions).

kate (cs): Heads up: CS has two customers who've messaged support about slow response times and timeouts (EnterpriseCorp and Chatly). I'm drafting a short note: "We're investigating elevated latency in a single AWS zone and routing traffic to other zones; minimal request loss expected." Will share once we have consistent metrics.

sam (oncall): Thanks Kate. Diego/olivia, after the NLB changes, what are we seeing on p95?

diego: After deregister/drain on 9 hosts, p95 dropped from 2.3s -> 560ms in 40s. Resolver timeouts reduced after TTL change; some residual RX drops on 3 hosts.

incident-bot: Update: Pagerduty duplicate suppressed, incident status -> mitigated (partial).

olivia: I'm going to kick KV cache warmers in eu-west2 to reduce cold start regressions due to traffic shift. Running: `curl -X POST https://ops.internal/kv-warmer?pool=g5-eu-west2`

sam (oncall): Diego, can you run `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids [ids]` for the three noisy ENIs and check secondary IP counts/attach state? Also check host kernel tx/rx drops.

diego: Running now. Output shows two ENIs with high `promiscuity` flags and `Attachment: attached`. No `Attach`/`Detach` churn logged. Kernel shows intermittent `skb_alloc_fallback` warnings. Might be driver-level jitter.

olivia: We've kept canary traffic routed to az1b for monitoring; p95 there is still ~720ms but stable. Overall traffic shifted ~22% to eu-west2. No customer errors ramping after reroute.

kate (cs): Sent preliminary message to EnterpriseCorp and Chatly: short note + link to status page. Both asked for ETA; I'll loop back once we have root cause.

eng-sre-oncall: Proposal: schedule a rolling kernel/driver update for the affected host images, but that's a post-incident action. For now we'll continue traffic steering and drain the 3 hosts to repro pool for deeper debugging.

sam (oncall): Agreed. Next steps: 1) Keep affected hosts drained. 2) Leave fallback weight to eu-west2 for 30m then ramp back. 3) Collect packet captures on drained hosts and handoff to hardware driver team. 4) Customer comms update in 10m.

incident-bot: Reminder: oncall handoff at 09:45 UTC scheduled. sam (oncall) initiating formal handoff to olivia in 30m.

olivia: 09:40 update: p95 global back to baseline ~220ms, az1b still slightly elevated but stable. I'll own the post-incident for RCA. Dropping DNS TTL back to 300s after stabilization.

kate (cs): Customer update posted: "We've rerouted traffic and reduced impact. If you continue to see errors, please open a ticket and we'll prioritize." Customers acknowledged. :thumbsup:

diego: Captures saved to s3://redwood-incidents/6132468101/pcap.tar.gz. Added pointer to ticket. Initial analysis points to sporadic RX queue growth under sustained small-packet bursts. We'll validate NIC driver and host interrupts.

sam (oncall): Thanks team. Incident status -> resolved (mitigated, root cause pending). Handoff to olivia for RCA and postmortem. Please add any follow-ups to the incident board.

olivia: Will file postmortem and include mitigations: better NLB draining defaults, faster fallback ramp, and host-level health heuristics (rx-queue threshold alert).

eng-sre-oncall: Adding runbook item: when ENI Rx queue > 60% AND resolver p50 > 100ms, automatically shift 20% traffic away for 10m.

kate (cs): Closing customer threads, will send summary to affected accounts once postmortem is ready.

sam (oncall): Leaving note: Pager closed at 09:48 UTC. Good job everyone. :heart:

(End of thread)
